limitations: Do not represent SCUBE2 as an autonomous VEGFR2 ligand; preserve the VEGF-dependent coreceptor interpretation, endothelial/ischemia model context, unresolved intracellular sequence and absent terminal-TF/target-gene evidence.

injury_context: Vascular angiogenesis comparator evidence only; no SCI transfer inferred
context_scope: Primary evidence supports alpha6beta1-dependent endothelial attachment to the laminin alpha4 G-domain and a functional angiogenesis context. The route is retained at the ligand/receptor/output layer without an intracellular, TF or target-gene claim.

citation_note: Primary laminin alpha4 G-domain integrin and endothelial angiogenesis study
evidence_summary: The primary study shows that the laminin alpha4 G-domain supports endothelial adhesion and that beta1/alpha6 blockade reduces attachment; the same domain is functionally important in a chimeric angiogenesis model. The route is retained as a bounded matrix-ligand-to-integrin-to-output annotation.
limitations: Preserve the cooperative/blockade semantics and distinguish direct high-affinity alphaVbeta3/alpha3beta1 binding from the alpha6beta1-dependent functional contribution; do not infer direct binary alpha6beta1 affinity, autonomous integrin signaling, terminal TF, target gene or SCI transfer.
